audioReceipts.caption: Slow glass-like tones drift through the light garden.
Air moving through glass reeds and a soft mechanical garden ventilation bed.
Footsteps on fine gravel
Connector cleaned; inspection still required
Photon highlights the optical connection
Start with the connector inspection. A dramatic theory can wait while we look for an ordinary defect.
Use the inspection equipment. Never look directly into a live optical port or fiber end.
The optic and the fiber must match the supplied profile. A pleasing glow is not a compatibility test.
Single mode and multiple modes describe light propagation. They do not promise one or several independent payload channels.
I can illuminate the connection. Delivering electrical power through that fiber is outside my job description.
After a change, inspect and measure again. The old reading can stay in the notebook as history.
Low resonant glass tone with occasional mechanical shutter breath.
Optical filter position changed
Measurement taken; inspect values and freshness
Measurement outside the stated range
Compare the received level with both receiver bounds, then check the required reserve margin.
An adequate optical budget cannot rescue an incompatible optic and fiber pair. Check both.
D B M is a power level. D B expresses a difference or ratio. Keep their labels attached to the numbers.
Above sensitivity is not the whole test. Leave the stated reserve margin, and do not exceed the stated maximum receive level.
Unicorn compares the single-mode profile
Hydra illustrates multiple propagation modes
